u0: No outstanding obligations at the moment: the siren is silent, no client is waiting with an untaken order, no food is being carried toward a pending preparation or serve, and no food has just slipped. The shop is in its neutral baseline, ready for the next event; from here a ring, a client arrival, a fall, or any other event opens the corresponding obligation.
u1: The siren has been handled and no order work is pending, but the siren is still ringing and must be silenced by toggling the switch. Until the switch is toggled, the ring remains an open obligation; otherwise the shop is again at rest.
u10: Prepared food has slipped out of the hands after an order was taken. The food must be picked back up so it can be served; the client's order is still unserved and remains an open obligation.
u11: Prepared food has slipped away while the siren is ringing untoggled and an order is already taken. Recovering the food, silencing the siren, and eventually serving the client are all still required.
u12: A new client has just arrived at the counter. Their order has not been taken yet, so the next required action is to take it; after that, food must be fetched, prepared at the stove, and served. The siren is quiet at this moment.
u13: A new client has just arrived while the siren is ringing and the switch is untoggled. The arrival's order must be taken and then fulfilled through fetch, prepare, and serve, and the siren must be silenced with the switch; both obligations are open.
u14: A client has arrived and food has been prepared, but no order is recorded as taken. Preparing only works for a waiting ordered client, so this is a transient combination; the machine's expectations are that the client's order still needs taking and any prepared food still needs serving to complete the visit. The siren is quiet.
u15: A client has arrived and food has been prepared while the siren rings untoggled. The customer's order is still not taken, so taking the order and serving the prepared food remain ahead, and the siren still needs silencing.
u16: A client has arrived and food has just slipped away; the order is not yet taken. The dropped food must be picked back up on the next move, and the new client's order must be taken and then fulfilled through preparation and service.
u17: A client has arrived and food has slipped while the siren is ringing untoggled, with no order taken. Recovering the food, taking the arriving client's order, and silencing the siren are all outstanding.
u18: A client has arrived, food has been prepared, and it has just slipped and not been recovered. The dropped food must be picked back up; the client's order still needs to be taken and then served, so several obligations are open at once.
u19: A client arrived while the siren rings untoggled, food has slipped, and food was prepared. Recovery of the dropped food is required, the siren must be silenced, and the arriving client's order still needs taking, preparing, and serving.
u2: A client's order has been taken and no food preparation is pending yet. The next required step is to fetch food from the pantry and prepare it at the stove; the siren is quiet for now, but if it starts ringing the switch must be handled too.
u20: A client who arrived earlier has had their order taken, and no food has been prepared yet. The order still needs food prepared at the stove and then served to the client; meanwhile any siren that rings must be switched off. The food has not slipped, and the siren is quiet right now, so nothing else is pending besides finishing the order and reacting to future rings.
u21: A client's order has been taken, no food has been prepared yet, and the siren is currently ringing. Turning the switch off promptly is required, and the order still needs preparing at the stove and serving; the food has not slipped. Finishing the ring response and the two remaining order steps are the outstanding tasks.
u22: A client's order was taken and no food has been prepared, but the food then slipped from the hands, so it must be picked up on the very next step. The siren is quiet at the moment, so the immediate demand is to regain the food and avoid a fatal miss. After that the order still needs preparing and serving, and any new ring must be silenced.
u23: A client's order is taken and no food is prepared, the food has just slipped, and the siren is ringing. The food must be picked up on the very next step, and the ringing siren must be switched off. After those, the order still needs preparing at the stove and serving.
u24: A client's order has been taken and the food is prepared, but the client has not been served yet and the siren is quiet. Serving the prepared food to the waiting client is the remaining order task, alongside switching off any siren that starts. The food has not slipped, so the hands are still full of the prepared portion.
u25: A client's order is taken and the food is prepared, but the client has not been served, and the siren is currently ringing. The siren must be switched off, and the prepared food must still be handed to the client. The food has not slipped.
u26: A client's order is taken and the food is prepared but not yet served; the prepared food then slipped, so it must be picked up on the very next step. The siren is quiet right now. After regaining the food, the client still needs to be served, and any new ring must be silenced.
u27: A client's order is taken and the food is prepared but not yet served, the prepared food has just slipped, and the siren is ringing. Picking the food up on the very next step and switching the siren off are the immediate demands. Serving the waiting client remains to be done afterwards.
u28: A mandatory requirement has been broken: after food slipped, it was not back in hand on the very next step, so the promise to recover it immediately can never be fulfilled. Successful completion is no longer possible and the task is failed.
u29: A client has just arrived at the counter and their order has not been taken yet; the siren is quiet. Taking that client's order is required, and after that food must be fetched, prepared at the stove and served. Any siren that starts must be switched off.
u3: A client's order has been taken while the siren is ringing and the switch has not yet been toggled. Two obligations are open: silence the siren with the switch, and fetch and prepare food for the waiting client. Both must eventually be fulfilled.
u30: A client has just arrived and their order has not been taken, while the siren is ringing. The siren must be switched off and the new client's order taken, after which fetching, preparing and serving the food remains. Both the ring response and the order steps are outstanding.
u31: A new client arrived and no order was taken, and the food then slipped from the hands, so it must be picked up on the very next step. The siren is quiet at the moment. After the pickup the client's order still needs taking, and the full fetch-prepare-serve flow follows, with any ring to be silenced.
u32: A new client arrived and no order was taken, the food has just slipped, and the siren is ringing. The food must be picked up on the very next step and the siren switched off. The client's order still needs taking, then the food prepared and served.
u4: Food has just been prepared for the waiting client and must still be handed over to them. The next required step is to serve the prepared food; the siren is quiet, so the only outstanding obligation is completing the service.
u5: Food has just been prepared while the siren is ringing and the switch has not been toggled. The prepared food still needs to be served to the client, and the siren still needs to be silenced; both obligations remain open.
u6: Food has just slipped out of the hands and was not yet recovered on the following step. The food must be picked up again; the machine still allows this before declaring failure, so regaining the carried food is the immediate priority, and once that happens the shop returns to its neutral state.
u7: Food has slipped and the siren is ringing with the switch untoggled. Recovery of the dropped food is required, and the siren must also be silenced; picking the food back up closes one obligation, leaving the siren still to handle.
u8: Food has slipped after an order was already taken. The immediate priority is to pick the dropped food back up again on the following step to restore carrying; once recovered, the order still needs its food prepared at the stove and ultimately served.
u9: Food has slipped after an order was taken and while the siren is ringing untoggled. The dropped food must be recovered, and both the siren and the client's order (fetch, prepare, serve) remain outstanding.
